one_shot.rationale: Kalista posts a slightly elevated win rate (51.4% global, 52.2% KR) on a very low pick rate of about 2.1-2.3%. That pattern usually comes from a small pool of dedicated, mechanically demanding players rather than genuine overtuning. Pro presence is moderate at 16%, which is not dominant enough to force a change. Ban rate is negligible, so players do not see her as oppressive. Nerfing would likely push an already niche pick out of solo queue. Hold and monitor whether pro presence climbs next patch.

Azir is slightly underperforming everywhere: about 49% win rate globally and 48.5% in Korea, with only 7% pro presence. Part of the low win rate is his difficulty curve, so a small, targeted buff to his core damage source is enough. This raises W soldier base damage by a flat 5 per rank. It helps lane consistency and sustained DPS without spiking his pro power through ratios or the R and E utility.

Global win rate is healthy at 50.4%, but Korea Emerald+ sits at 54.3% over a solid sample (~8.7k games), and pro presence is 11%. This suggests she overperforms in skilled hands. A light trim to Q's later-rank base damage reduces her mid-game burst, where skilled players snowball most. Early laning and her low global pick rate are left intact. Only one field changes, and every rank stays within 20% of its current value.

Azir is under 50% win rate in both regions, at 49.2% globally and 48.75% in KR. Some of that is his skill floor. He also has low solo queue pick rate and only 8% pro presence, which is unusually low for a champion normally kept in check by pro play. A small flat buff to soldier base damage strengthens his early laning and wave clear without scaling into late-game AP spikes. This lifts solo queue performance modestly and keeps pro risk controlled, since the ratios are unchanged.

Kalista sits at about 50.7% global and 50.9% KR win rate on healthy samples (88k and 23k games). Her pick rate is low, as is typical for a high-skill niche ADC, and her ban rate is minimal. Pro presence of 21% is moderate and not dominant, so there's no pro-play pressure to nerf. Solo queue performance is balanced and pro play isn't warped, so no change is warranted this patch.

proposal.rationale: Lee Sin is overperforming in high-elo solo queue (KR 52.5% WR with 54% ban rate) while holding 43% pro presence, so he's strong across the board. We're taking a light pass at his core damage rather than his identity: Sonic Wave base damage goes from 60/90/120/150/180 to 55/82/110/137/165 (about -8% at every rank) and base AD drops from 66 to 64. Together these trim his early skirmish and gank damage (roughly -2% lane trade) and slightly shave his late damage, without touching the Insec/kick utility or the mobility that defines the champion. Sim: soloq index -0.73%, pro index -0.34%, both within target.

one_shot.rationale: Lee Sin is overperforming for a high-skill jungler. He has a 51.3% global and 52.5% KR win rate on large samples, a 26% pick rate and 54% ban rate in KR, and 43% pro presence. Win rates this high on such a mechanically demanding champion point to excess power, likely concentrated in his early skirmishing. Trimming base damage on both Q casts lowers his early ganks, clears and kill pressure without touching his ult-based playmaking or his mobility identity. Ratios stay intact, so built-up Lee Sin still scales. The cut grows from 5 damage at rank 1 to 10 at max rank, about a 5-8% damage reduction.

proposal.rationale: Viego is popular but losing in solo queue, especially in KR (48.9% WR at 7% pick rate), and he barely shows up in pro play (1% presence). He needs more early and mid-game strength without boosting his late-game, coordinated power. Base AD 57 -> 61 makes his early clears and lane trades stronger. Q base damage goes up at ranks 1-3 only (25/40/55 -> 30/45/60), with ranks 4-5 unchanged. That front-loads the buff into the early game, when solo queue games are decided, and his late-game ceiling stays where it is. Sim: soloq_index +0.85% (target 0.5–3%), pro_index +0.29% (cap 1%).

one_shot.rationale: Solo queue Viego is balanced to slightly weak: 50.5% global win rate, 48.9% in Korea, with moderate pick and ban rates. Pro presence is 100%, though, which points to a pro-play problem. The main driver is likely Heartbreaker's reliable engage and reset value in coordinated teamfights. A modest increase to R's cooldown at every rank means fewer ults per objective fight, which hits structured play hardest. Solo queue should be less affected, since games there are less ult-cycle dependent, so his core skirmishing and clear (Q/E) are left untouched given the already-low Korean win rate.

proposal.rationale: Garen is winning too much in solo queue (53.2% WR globally, 7% pick) while having zero pro presence, so we want to take power out of his lane without touching his late game. His lane dominance comes from early Judgment (E) spins: max-first E lets him win extended trades from levels 1-6. We lower Judgment's early-rank damage (AD ratio 0.40/0.43/0.46 -> 0.34/0.38/0.43, base 4/7/10/13 -> 3.5/6/9/12.5) while leaving rank 5 untouched. This cuts his level-6 trade damage by ~5% (soloq index -1.2%, mid-band) and leaves late DPS, siege, and utility unchanged, so his pro/late-game power isn't reduced (pro index +0.8%). We didn't use base HP because the sim showed it had no effect, and we didn't use base AD because it also lowers late-game DPS.

one_shot.rationale: Garen is overperforming in solo queue: 53.2% WR globally on a 7% pick rate across 200k+ games, and 52.2% in KR. Pro presence is zero, so there is no competitive play to protect, and solo queue alone justifies a nerf. The cut targets his core sustained damage rather than his defenses, so he keeps his identity as a beginner-friendly juggernaut. E's per-spin AD ratio drops by 0.02 at every rank, which weakens his signature spin trades and all-ins. A small base AD cut, 69 to 67, softens early lane pressure and Q/E scaling. Both changes are modest, around 3-5%, aiming to pull win rate toward about 51% without gutting him.

Qiyana is over-performing: 51.8% global WR rising to 54.2% in Korea Emerald+, plus 18% pro presence. The Korea gap suggests skilled players are getting outsized value from her burst pattern. A light trim to Q base damage, shaved mostly from early ranks, lowers her lane and skirmish pressure without touching her identity or her ultimate's teamfight ceiling. The hit is about 12% at rank 1 and 5% at max rank.

Azir sits below 49% win rate both globally (48.95%) and in Korea (48.71%). That is somewhat low even for a high-skill champion. His pick rate is modest and pro presence is only 2%, so neither solo queue nor pro play justifies holding him down. A small buff to soldier attack base damage improves his laning and sustained DPS without touching his ultimate or mobility, which are the parts that would make him oppressive in pro play. Leaving the AP ratios alone keeps his late-game ceiling unchanged.

Lee Sin is overperforming across every tier we track. In Korea he has a 52.4% win rate on 25.6% pick and 55.6% ban, globally he holds 50.9% on 13.3% pick, and pro presence is 44%. He is strong both in the hands of skilled players and in raw solo queue win rate, so a targeted nerf is warranted. Trimming Q base damage on both casts lowers his early-game gank and skirmish pressure, which drives his pro and high-elo value. His bonus AD scaling stays intact so late-game mastery payoff is preserved. The cut grows with rank, from 5 at rank 1 to 10 at max rank (about 8% at rank 1 and under 6% at max), so it stays well within the 20% limit.

proposal.rationale: Garen is overperforming in solo queue (53.2% WR global, 52.7% KR) while being essentially absent from pro play (1% presence). His strength is in lane: early trades and spinning-to-win before items come online. We're trimming that early pressure without touching what defines him late: base AD 69 -> 66 makes his early autos and Q/E trades weaker in lane, and Judgment's early-rank base damage is reduced (4/7/10/13/16 -> 3.2/6/9/12.5/16) so maxing E first is less oppressive while rank 5 is unchanged. Ratios, ultimate, W and late-rank values are untouched, so his late-game/coordinated power (pro) stays where it is. Sim: soloq_index -0.98% (target -3% to -0.5%), pro_index +0.21% (target >= -0.5%).

one_shot.rationale: Garen is overperforming at Emerald+ in both regions: 53.2% WR globally on a 7.2% pick rate and 52.7% in Korea. Pro presence is minimal, so this is a pure solo queue problem. Most of that strength comes from sustained Judgment damage in extended trades. I'm trimming E's AD ratio at every rank and taking a little early Decisive Strike base damage. That softens lane and teamfight output without touching his defensive identity. Expected result is roughly a 1-1.5% win rate drop.

Kalista is healthy in solo queue, at 50.7% global and 51.6% KR. Those win rates sit on a low pick rate dominated by experienced players, so they don't signal overperformance. Pro presence of 33% is notable but not dominant for a champion historically valued in organized play. Any nerf to her damage or base stats would mostly hurt solo queue, where she is not a problem. Hold and monitor pro presence; if it climbs toward 60%+, consider a targeted change to Fate's Call or early E scaling.

Viego sits at 51.24% win rate globally on a 9.5% pick rate, which is slightly above average. In Korea Emerald+ he is at 50.39%, which is balanced, and his Korean ban rate is low at 1.83%. Pro presence is minimal at 3%, so there is no competitive pressure to act. The global edge is modest, and with skilled Korean players he looks healthy, so a change risks overcorrecting. Hold and monitor the global win rate for another patch.

Globally Lee Sin is balanced, with a 50.5% win rate at 13% pick rate. In Korea Emerald+ he is overperforming: 52% win rate, 25.5% pick rate and a 56.7% ban rate, alongside 57% pro presence. That pattern suggests he is strongest in skilled hands, so a light nerf is warranted. Trimming Sonic Wave's flat base damage by 5 at every rank cuts into his early ganks and clears, the source of his pro and high-elo priority. The 0.9 bonus AD ratio is untouched, so late-game outplay potential stays intact. A flat cut makes the relative reduction largest early (about 8% at rank 1), which limits the risk of overshooting his lower-elo balance.

proposal.rationale: Viego is played a lot but underperforms in solo queue (KR WR 48.8% at 6.7% PR), while pro presence is already low and doesn't need help. We're buffing his early game through Blade of the Ruined King: more Q base damage at early and mid ranks, and more %current-HP on-hit at ranks 1-4. Rank 5 on-hit is unchanged. This makes his early clears, ganks and skirmishes stronger, which is where solo queue Viego struggles. His late-game ceiling, ratios, ultimate and utility stay the same, so coordinated/pro play is barely affected (sim: soloq +0.95%, pro -0.2%).

one_shot.rationale: Viego is healthy globally at 50.35% WR with high pick rate (8.83%) across 257k games, so performance is solidly balanced. Korea's 48.82% is slightly low but within the normal range for a mechanically demanding jungler in a high-skill region. The 1.32% ban rate there suggests no frustration. Pro presence of 2% is low but not concerning for a solo-queue-oriented reset champion. No change is warranted.

Azir sits below 49% WR both globally (48.9%) and in KR (48.4%). His pick rate is low, ban rate is negligible and pro presence is only 2%, so he isn't being held back to protect pro play. Some of the low win rate comes from his difficulty, but he is underperforming in every setting. A small buff to the base damage of his main damage tool, the soldier attack (W), helps his weak early laning and wave clear. It leaves his late-game AP scaling and pro-play utility (R wall, E engage) untouched, so he shouldn't jump into pro dominance.

Kalista is overperforming for a mechanically demanding, low-pick champion: 51% global WR, 52% in KR, and 33% pro presence. A light nerf to the flat per-spear Rend damage trims her early lane and objective-securing power, which is where pro play leans on her. Her late-game AD-ratio scaling stays intact, so the change is measured rather than gutting her.

proposal.rationale: Garen is winning too much in solo queue (52.8% global, 53.3% KR) with zero pro presence, so the problem is his early-lane bullying rather than his late-game or coordinated value. We're toning down his laning: base AD 69 -> 66 and Judgment (E) base damage at ranks 1-3 from 4/7/10 to 3.2/5.6/8 (ranks 4-5 unchanged). This makes his early spins and level 6 trades weaker (lane trade -5.5%) while leaving his late-game spin damage and ultimate untouched, so he isn't pushed further out of pro play. Sim: soloq_index -1.3%, pro_index +0.45%, both inside their target bands.

one_shot.rationale: Garen is winning about 53% of solo queue games both globally (52.8% across ~167k games) and in Korea (53.3%), with a healthy 6.8% global pick rate. That is clearly above the balance band. He has zero pro presence, so this nerf can target solo queue directly with no pro-play risk. His strength comes from sustained E (Judgment) damage. Trimming the E AD ratio by 0.02 at every rank lowers his damage output, especially with AD items, without touching his core tankiness or identity. Q and R stay intact.

Viego is slightly overperforming in global solo queue, with a 51.2% win rate at an 8.6% pick rate over a large sample. Korea is balanced at 50.1%, and pro presence is minimal at 3%, so the case for action is modest. A light trim to Q base damage targets his early clear and dueling, where most of his low-to-mid elo strength comes from. It leaves his ratio-driven late game and pro-relevant reset kit untouched. The change is about 5 damage per rank, which should pull the global win rate toward 50% without hurting the balanced Korean numbers much.

proposal.rationale: Qiyana is strong across the board: 53.8% WR in KR solo queue and 61% pro presence. Edge of Ixtal is her core damage tool from the first trade through late-game skirmishes, so one targeted nerf to it addresses both. The flat base damage cut (-10 at all ranks) trims her early lane trades and solo-queue snowball. The bonus AD ratio cut (0.9 -> 0.8) lowers her itemized late-game burst, which is where pro play gets its value. Players will read this as a single, clear "Q hits a little less hard" change. Her elemental utility, mobility and ultimate engage stay untouched, so her identity is preserved. Sim: soloq_index -0.90%, pro_index -0.44%, both inside the target bands.

one_shot.rationale: Qiyana is overperforming on every axis: 51.6% WR globally, 53.8% in Korea with a 10.7% ban rate, and 61% pro presence. A nerf is clearly warranted. Her power is concentrated in burst from the Q into R combo, so trimming Q's base damage across all ranks (more at early ranks) cuts lane pressure and early skirmish lethality. It leaves the AD ratios that define her scaling and assassin identity intact. This is a moderate hit rather than a gutting, since her pick rate is low and the high win rate partly reflects specialist play.

Lee Sin is overperforming on every axis. He wins 50.81% globally on a 12.8% pick rate and 52.21% in Korea with a 24.5% pick rate and 56% ban rate, and he holds 57% pro presence. Winning above 50% while this popular, and especially in the highest-skill region, points to excess power rather than a mastery-driven win rate. Because his strength concentrates in the early skirmishes Q enables, the change trims 5 base damage per rank from both halves of Q (Sonic Wave and Resonating Strike), each under 9% of the current value. This takes the edge off early ganks and the execute without touching his mobility or Insec playmaking.

Azir is under 49% win rate both globally (48.45%) and in Korea (48.88%), with a low ~1.8-1.9% pick rate and no pro presence, so he is weak at every level of play. Pro play usually holds his power down, but with 0% presence there is room for a modest solo queue buff. Soldier attacks (W) are his core sustained damage, so a small flat W base damage increase helps his laning and DPS without making Shurima Shuffle burst more oppressive. Q base gets a light early-rank bump to ease the laning phase.

Kalista sits at a healthy 50.7% win rate globally and 51.5% in Korea on large samples, with moderate pick and ban rates. Pro presence of 22% is reasonable for a high-skill, pro-favored ADC and isn't dominant. Neither the solo queue nor the pro data shows a clear outlier, so her numbers stay unchanged this patch and we keep monitoring.

Viego sits at 51.0% win rate globally on a healthy 8.4% pick rate, and 49.75% in Korea. That spread suggests skilled players aren't over-performing on him. Ban rate is moderate and pro presence is zero, so he isn't distorting competitive play. Nothing is clearly out of line, so no changes this patch; keep monitoring.

proposal.rationale: Garen is winning too much in solo queue (52.8% global, 53.0% KR) and isn't played in pro at all (0% presence). The problem is how hard he hits in lane, not how he does late. So this patch cuts his early damage and leaves his late game alone. Base AD goes from 69 to 66, which makes his early autos, Q and E trades weaker. The lower ranks of Judgment (E) lose some base damage per spin (4/7/10/13 -> 3.2/6/9/12.5), and the max rank stays at 16. Garen maxes E first, so this weakens the early spin trades that win his lane without changing how strong the ability is at max rank. In the sim, solo queue power drops about 1.0% (target band -3% to -0.5%). Pro power stays flat to slightly up (+0.2%, target is no lower than -0.5%), so his already low pro presence isn't hurt any further.

one_shot.rationale: Garen is overperforming in both regions, with about 52.8% win rate globally and 53.0% in Korea, plus healthy pick rates. He has no pro presence, so a solo-queue-targeted nerf carries no competitive risk. I'm trimming his E AD ratio across all ranks and shaving 2 base AD. This lowers his early trades and his sustained spin damage in lane without touching his identity: Q silence, W tankiness, R execute. The goal is to pull him toward a 50-51% win rate.

Lee Sin is over-performing at every level. Global winrate is 50.79% on a high pick rate. In Korea he sits at 52.45% WR with 24.65% pick and 56% ban. Pro presence is 54%. A targeted cut to Q damage, his main early skirmish and execute tool, trims early-game power and kill pressure without touching his mobility identity. The flat 5 is a larger relative cut at low ranks (8% at rank 1, under 3% at rank 5), so it mostly hits early ganks and invades.

proposal.rationale: Qiyana is strong at both ends: 54.5% WR in KR solo queue alongside 61% pro presence. Two targeted nerfs: (1) Edge of Ixtal (Q) base damage reduced by 15 at all ranks (80-200 -> 65-185). This trims her lane trading and early skirmish burst, which is the main lever for solo queue power. (2) Supreme Display of Talent (R) bonus AD ratio 125% -> 110%. This lowers her late-game teamfight one-shot potential, which coordinated pro play gets the most out of, while keeping the ultimate's identity (stun, % max HP) intact. Sim: soloq_index -0.88%, pro_index -0.39%, both inside the target bands.

one_shot.rationale: Qiyana is overperforming across the board: 51.6% win rate globally, 54.5% in KR Emerald+, and 61% pro presence. That points to a kit that is too strong at both skill levels, not just a pro-play problem. Her low pick rate keeps the change modest, so this trims her most frequent damage source, Q Edge of Ixtal, mostly at higher ranks. That cuts the burst and execute damage of her repeated trades and all-ins. Early damage is barely touched, and R plus her mobility are left alone, so her identity and playmaking stay intact.

Azir sits slightly below 50% in both regions (49.0% global, 48.78% KR) on healthy sample sizes. Some of that gap reflects his high skill floor. Still, 0% pro presence for a champion who is normally a pro staple suggests he is underpowered at the high end too. A modest buff to W soldier base damage raises his core sustained DPS and lane pressure without touching his E/R engage pattern, so it helps both solo queue and pro play without risking a power spike.

proposal.rationale: Garen is over-performing in solo queue (52.7% global, 53.5% KR WR) with zero pro presence, so this is a pure early/lane-power problem. Judgment (E) is his main laning trade tool and he maxes it first, so we trim its base damage on ranks 1-3 only (4/7/10 -> 3.2/5.6/8), leaving ranks 4-5 and the AD ratios untouched. A 1-point base AD shave (69 -> 68) slightly softens level-1 trades and early last-hitting. Sim: lane trade at L6 drops ~3.7%, soloq_index -0.86%; late DPS and siege are essentially unchanged and pro_index stays flat/slightly up, so his late-game and pro viability are not hurt.

one_shot.rationale: Garen is overperforming with a 52.7% global and 53.5% KR win rate at Emerald+ and a healthy 6.2% global pick rate. He has no pro presence, so this is purely a solo queue adjustment. His strength comes from Judgment's sustained damage in extended trades and all-ins, so trimming E's AD scaling slightly reduces his lane bullying and teamfight spin damage without touching his tankiness or his execute identity. The change is small (about 4-5% per rank) to bring him toward about 51% without gutting a popular low-elo staple.

Kalista sits at a healthy 50.5% global and 51.3% KR win rate on a modest 4.8-5.1% pick rate. Her pro presence of 22% is notable but not oppressive. Low-pick, high-skill marksmen naturally post slightly elevated win rates from their dedicated players, so neither number signals a problem. Changing her solo queue numbers risks destabilizing a champion who is performing within target bands, so we hold and keep monitoring pro presence.

Viego is slightly over-performing in global Emerald+ solo queue: 51.5% WR on 8.26% pick rate across a large sample. He is closer to balanced in Korea (50.44%) and has no pro presence, so only a light solo-queue nerf is warranted. Trimming Q base damage slightly lowers early skirmish and clear power without touching his scaling identity, the on-hit damage or the reset pattern.

proposal.rationale: Qiyana is strong across the board: 54.8% WR in KR with 57% pro presence. Edge of Ixtal is her main damage tool in both lane trades and late-game teamfight burst, so we're toning down this one ability rather than spreading nerfs across her kit. Base damage -15 at all ranks hits her early lane trading and solo queue snowballing hardest. Bonus AD ratio 0.9 -> 0.8 trims her itemized late burst, which is what keeps her a pick in pro play. In simulation solo queue power drops ~1.2% and pro power drops ~0.5%, both comfortably inside the targets. Her mobility, elemental utility and ult are unchanged, so she plays the same way.

one_shot.rationale: Qiyana is overperforming across every tier we track: 51.5% global WR, 54.8% in KR (Emerald+), and 57% pro presence. A strong win rate on a low-pickrate, high-skill assassin points to excessive burst in skilled hands. Trimming Q base damage by a flat 10 at every rank cuts her laning trades and her Q/E/R kill combo without touching her mobility or terrain utility, which are what make her competitive play distinctive. A small trim to R's bonus AD ratio lowers late-game one-shot potential, which matters in pro play and high-elo KR.

proposal.rationale: Garen is winning too much in solo queue (52.9% global WR, 6.3% pick rate) while having no pro presence, so the problem is his early lane pressure, not his late-game or teamfight value. Lowering base AD from 69 to 64 weakens his early trades and all-ins (level 6 lane trade drops by about 5%) and barely touches his late game, because items make up most of his damage by then. In the sim, soloq_index moves -1.1%, inside the -0.5% to -3% target, and pro_index is basically flat at -0.03%, above the -0.5% floor. It's a one-number change that players will easily understand: Garen hits a little softer in lane.

one_shot.rationale: Garen is sitting at about 52.9% win rate globally and 52.4% in Korea at Emerald+, with healthy pick rate and zero pro presence. That makes him a solo-queue outlier, and pro play gives no reason to protect him. Trim his sustained damage through E's AD ratio (about 4-5% per rank), which is the core of his lane and teamfight output. Q burst, W tankiness and R execute stay untouched so his identity and counterplay are preserved. A light, single-lever nerf should pull his win rate toward 51% without pushing him out of the meta.

proposal.rationale: Qiyana is strong overall: 52.5%+ win rate in high-elo KR solo queue alongside 57% pro presence. Edge of Ixtal is her core damage tool both in lane and in late-game assassinations, so we're toning it down across the board: base damage -10 at all ranks hits her lane trades and early skirmishes (solo queue), while the bonus AD ratio 0.9 -> 0.8 trims her itemized late-game burst that pro teams rely on. Her mobility, ult engage and elemental utility are untouched, so her identity stays intact — she just kills a bit less reliably with Q.

one_shot.rationale: Global solo queue WR is healthy at 50.07%. Korea Emerald+ sits at 52.5% and pro presence is 57%, which suggests she overperforms in coordinated, high-skill play. Her ultimate's terrain-reliant engage and burst drive her teamfight value in organized games. A modest R cooldown increase targets that engage uptime while barely affecting her lane or skirmish power in solo queue.

proposal.rationale: Lee Sin is popular but underperforming in global solo queue (49.47% WR at 12.4% PR), while pro presence is already high (54%) so we must not add late-game or coordinated power. We buff his early game only: Sonic Wave and Resonating Strike base damage go up at ranks 1-3 (60/90/120 -> 72/105/130), with ranks 4-5 untouched, plus +2 base AD (66 -> 68) to make his level 1-6 trades and early clears feel better. No ratios, late ranks, cooldowns or utility (R, W shield, E slow) are touched, so his late scaling and pro value stay flat. Sim: soloq_index +1.13% (target +0.5% to +3%), pro_index -0.18% (target at most +1%).

one_shot.rationale: Lee Sin is strong in coordinated, high-skill play but balanced overall. Korea shows a 50.76% win rate with a 48% ban rate, and pro presence is 54%. The global Emerald+ win rate, however, sits at 49.47% across a large 348k-game sample. That gap is the classic Lee Sin skill curve. Any general nerf to damage, cooldowns or energy would push the broad population further below 50% without clearly fixing pro priority. Hold this patch and watch whether pro presence climbs further or the Korean win rate pushes past about 51.5% while staying heavily banned. If it does, consider a narrowly targeted change, such as the W_safeguard cooldown or Q base damage at early ranks, that hits coordinated play more than solo queue.
